newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Unidare warns profits below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Unidare warns profits below expectations.

text.p: Unidare Plc on Friday warned that continuing slow growth and tight margins in the company's welding businesses will result in operating profits being below current market expectations.

It also announced that it had completed the sale of its plastics division to UP Holdings Ltd for a total cash consideration, before expenses and including repayment of inter-group loans, of about 5.3 million sterling.

Unidare said sales growth, which it had expected to be strong from January onwards, was weak, and considerable margin pressure was being experienced by the company's UK and U.S. welding distribution businesses.

"While some growth is being achieved, it remains less than planned and margins continue to disappoint," Unidare said. "These factors will lead operating profits for the year to September 30, 1996 to fall short of current market expectations."
Unidare said that despite these disappointments, it retained confidence in the outlook for the future and intended, "barring unforseen circumstances, to maintain the dividend in the current year".

The engineering group said the disposal of its plastics division brought the total cash realisation from the disposal and reorganisation programme of the last two years to approximately 18 million Irish pounds.

"The sale is in line with the company's strategy of concentrating on its two core business areas, the distribution of industrial consumables and the manufacture of niche heating and metal products," Unidare said in a statement.
